solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Amorous and sensual, topless, embracing chap

indicators.note: embracing means the trimmed word holds the next piece inside it
topless says the word for sensual loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: sensual means erotic
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A description of a passionate, half-naked lover holding a man close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' leaves ROTIC, and 'embracing' wraps it round the chap. 'Amorous and sensual' tempts as a two-word definition, but 'sensual' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone inclined to love and passion; a synonym pair.

clue.text: Overweight English lot

parts.note: overweight means fat

explanation.surface: Being overweight is presented as the lot of the English.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny or fortune in life, a synonym.

clue.text: Hunks and tarts consuming case of champagne

indicators.note: consuming means the pastries swallow the next piece inside them

parts.note: tarts are pies

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Muscular men and loose women downing champagne at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes champagne's outside letters and 'consuming' puts them in the pastries. 'Hunks' and 'tarts' read as people, but hunks are chunks and tarts are pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunks are large pieces or chunks of something, a synonym.

clue.text: Crimes among criminal traders

parts.note: of can mean among, as in 'one of many'
fences are dealers in stolen goods

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing is said to be common among dishonest dealers.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is a receiver who buys and sells stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are breaches of the law, a direct synonym for crimes.

clue.text: Wise men consider accepting street justice

indicators.note: accepting means the two words together take another piece in between

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity
to rate is to consider or judge

explanation.surface: Learned figures are asked to weigh up what justice on the streets means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' lets the wise men and the verb take the street between them; 'justice' is the title, as in Justice of the Peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice of the peace is a magistrate, so justice here is the title of a judicial officer.

clue.text: Country's party premier

parts.note: a do is a party
premier means main, chief

explanation.surface: A nation's leading political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' and 'premier' look like politics, but a do is a celebration and premier is an adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a realm or territory ruled by someone, so a country.

clue.text: Singer's cadenza ends in very old record

indicators.note: in places those end letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: a list is a record or register

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A singer's showy cadenza ends up on a very old recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes the outside letters of cadenza and 'in' slots them after very old, before the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is a person who sings, a direct synonym.

clue.text: It's not hard currency

definitions.meaning: soft, gentle or sore to the touch
money accepted in payment, as in legal money

explanation.definitionFit: The word means soft or delicate, and legal tender is accepted money.

clue.text: Criminal after fine, one almost in jug

indicators.note: after puts the criminal's word behind the letter for fine

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a lag is a convict, especially an old lag

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: one is the word itself, trimmed

explanation.surface: A villain, having been fined, is nearly put back in jug, that is, prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is slang for prison, which fits the criminal, but here it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large jug or bottle for wine or ale, a type of jug.

clue.text: Hamlet perhaps, desperate character chasing Ophelia's heart

indicators.note: chasing puts the first piece in front, the heart letter following behind

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strong-man character in the British comic The Dandy

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Hamlet, a desperate figure, pursues Ophelia's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a cowboy in the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, an example of a Danish person, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Inveterate criminal kind getting time

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: getting means the friendly word receives a letter inside it

parts.note: kind means genial, friendly

explanation.surface: A habitual offender, despite being nice, ends up doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenital means present from birth, so ingrained or habitual, like inveterate.

clue.text: Arrowroot, it isn't containing inflammation

indicators.note: containing says the answer sits inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: A claim that arrowroot has nothing inflammatory in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is the medical term for inflammation of the ear, an example of inflammation.

clue.text: Melodramatic hit act with Lear going mad

indicators.note: going mad signals the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A show-stopping act in which King Lear loses his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going mad' rearranges HITACT and LEAR. The surface points at King Lear's madness on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical behaviour is exaggerated and showy, a synonym for melodramatic.

clue.text: Going around light speed is sensational

indicators.note: around means the leaving word wraps about the next letter

parts.note: going means exiting, leaving
C is the physicist's symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Travelling round at the speed of light would be thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting and sensational both describe something thrilling, a synonym pair.

clue.text: It's hard when one's out of luck!

definitions.text: It's hard when one's out of luck!

parts.words: It's hard when one's out of luck!
parts.note: the phrase 'hard ...' is British slang for bad luck, and a hard variety of this food is what is meant

explanation.surface: A sympathetic remark that life is tough when your luck runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is a British expression of mock sympathy meaning 'bad luck'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue completes the British idiom 'hard cheese', meaning tough luck, while hard is also a kind of this dairy food.

clue.text: …ergo sum initially includes case for philosopher

indicators.note: includes means the pair of pieces holds the box inside

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: a crate is a case or box

explanation.surface: Following on from a previous clue, Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am' is extended to a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues the previous clue to form 'cogito ergo sum', Descartes' line. 'initially' takes the first letter of sum, and 'includes' wraps the pieces round the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian thinker of the fifth century BC, an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Getaway south in European peninsula

parts.note: a cape is a headland or peninsula

explanation.surface: A holiday escape to the south of a European peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a flight from captivity or danger, a synonym.

clue.text: Hazard from green and rough

indicators.note: rough signals the letters are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Golf: danger lurks between the green and the rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' and 'green' are golf terms, but 'rough' rearranges GREEN and AND; 'Hazard' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to put it at risk, a synonym for to endanger.

clue.text: Challenged, providing over in action

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the deed

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: over means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: providing means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A challenge made on condition that action follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the condition word backwards and 'in' places it inside the action.
explanation.definitionFit: To have defied someone is to have challenged or resisted them openly.

clue.text: Hitch cables to rock

indicators.note: rock means the letters are shaken into a different order

explanation.surface: Instructions to tie cables to a rock with a hitch knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' rearranges CABLES and TO. 'Hitch' suggests a knot, but here it is a snag.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or problem, a synonym for an obstacle.

clue.text: Opening of big estate for shoot

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a ranch is a large estate or farm

explanation.surface: The start of a shooting party on a large country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests a hunting party, but it is the plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot is new growth on a plant, as a branch is, a synonym.

clue.text: Atonement from dead's following last word

indicators.note: following puts the dead's letters behind the final word

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
D is the abbreviation for dead, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Making peace with the dead after the last word at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to make up for a wrong, which is atonement.

clue.text: Nearly American on 'Fifty-Second Street'

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece on top of the rest

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An American living on New York's Fifty-Second Street.
explanation.walkthrough: The street name is broken into L (Roman fifty), MO (a second) and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and nearly both mean not quite, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Control limits a free market economy

parts.note: to cap is to control or limit

indicators.note: free means the letters are set loose into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Putting controls in place limits a free market economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like part of 'free market economy' but rearranges LIMITSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalism is the economic system run by private enterprise and markets.

clue.text: Criminal proclivity?

definitions.meaning: slang for dishonest or corrupt, as a crooked copper
a natural leaning or inclination, as in a talent for something

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word is slang for corrupt; as a noun it means an inclination or aptitude.

clue.text: Starts to bellow out offensive sound

definitions.text: Starts to bellow out offensive sound

indicators.note: starts to signals the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Beginning to bellow out an insulting noise at a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the first letters and the definition: jeers bellowed out as an offensive sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeering noises of disapproval shouted at a performer are offensive sounds bellowed out.

clue.text: Crushed capers for jam

indicators.note: crushed means the letters are squashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Crushed capers used as a spread instead of jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' suggests the preserve, but it means a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, a jam, a synonym.

clue.text: Turn up record, 'Endless Love' by Queen

parts.note: a disc is a record

indicators.note: endless means the word loses both its end letters

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Finding a record of 'Endless Love' performed by the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves OV from LOVE. Queen suggests the rock band, but it is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up something is to find or uncover it, a phrasal synonym.
